{{Quote|Then there was the time I stalked a giant peko-peko for ten days. It got away, but for me it was all about the hunt, not the kill. Okay, okay. I really wish it hadn't gotten away. It would make for a better story.|[[Walker Luskeske]], to a spacer|<ref name="SWG:WL">{{SWGcite|exp=NGE|type=conversation|Walker Luskeske|Naboo}}</ref>}}
'''Peko-pekos''' were large, strong [[Reptavian/Legends|reptavians]], whose raucous squawks carried over long distances.<ref name=":0" /> They were native to the [[Gungan/Legends|Gungan]] [[Gungan Swamp|swamps]] of [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]].<ref name="TPM" /> Another breed lived on [[Nal Hutta/Legends|Nal Hutta]].<ref name="Hunt for Ziro">{{TCW|Hunt for Ziro}}</ref> The feathers of the peko-peko albatross were used in the construction of [[Reinforced Insulated Sheath armor]].<ref name="SWG:P4">{{SWGcite|exp=AED|type=other}}Publish 4</ref>

Impressively sized specimens were known as "Giant Peko-Pekos."<ref name="SWG:WL" />

==Characteristics==
[[File:Pekopeko-woswfg.jpg|thumb|left|180px|A peko-peko]]
Peko-pekos congregated in large flocks but generally traveled in pairs and mated for life. Both male and female had beautiful indigo-sapphire plumage, and both were the same size. Peko-pekos had powerful wings and fairly toxic skin and feathers. Most animals left peko-pekos alone, as their toxins caused sharp stomach pains, severe vomiting, and occasional deaths. Not all animals were susceptible, however.<ref name=":0" /> Ironically, the peko-peko's blood contained antivenin for [[glie]]-based poisons. They had keen eyesight, clawed wings to help them climb, and a powerful beak that could crush even the hardest of nuts.<ref name=":0">''[[The Wildlife of Star Wars: A Field Guide]]''</ref>

Besides nuts, the peko-peko ate [[Kaadu/Legends|kaadu]] eggs and small creatures. Certain nuts and seeds would not germinate unless they passed through the peko-peko's gastrointestinal system. They were preyed upon by [[tusk cat]]s.<ref name=":0" />

The peko-peko nested in the high hollows of trees. The female laid two [[Egg/Legends|eggs]] at a time. Both partners cared for hatchlings.<ref name=":0" /> Peko-peko couples are formed for life, and each couple lives in its private area, removed from the others. According to [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]] folklore, the rare sight of more than two peko-pekos flying together was a good omen.<ref name=":1">{{DB|creature|pekopeko|peko-peko}}</ref> [[The Nook]] [[Restaurant/Legends|diner]] on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] served [[peko peko egg omelet]]s.<ref name="Ascension" />

Skilled mimics, they imitated perfectly the sounds of many other animals. Easily taught to talk in captivity, they were a favorite pet of both [[Gungan/Legends|Gungans]] and [[Naboo (people)/Legends|Naboo]].<ref name=":0" />

The [[Alsakan/Legends|Alsakan]] outlaw [[Cornelius Evazan/Legends|Cornelius Evazan]] conducted experiments on peko-pekos which resulted in the creation of the mutated [[Toxic peko-peko]].<ref name="Card-SWGTCG-Toxic Peko-Peko Mount">{{SWGTCG|set=Agents of Deception|cardname=Toxic Peko-Peko Mount}}</ref>

The peko-peko's skin is toxic, and most predators leave it alone.<ref name=":0" /> Sentient hunters prey on the peko-peko to harvest the amazing anti-venin the animal secretes.<ref name=":1" /> Peko-peko meat was comestible. The cookbook ''[[Essential Cooking Skills]]'' detailed how to best cook that meat.<ref name="SWG:ECS">{{SWGcite|exp=AED|type=item|ESSENTIAL COOKING SKILLS}}</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
Concept artist [[Terryl Whitlatch]] developed the peko-peko's coloring from the terrestrial peacock and the hyacinth macaw. Its peculiar beak was designed to crack open large coconut-sized nuts. It has claws on its wings, like the South American hoatzin, which gives the bird added mobility in the treetop canopies of [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]].<ref name=":1" />
